title: DJAFER v. NORTH MACEDONIA
summary: In the case of Djafer v. North Macedonia, the applicant, Ms. Sofija Djafer, was represented by the European Roma Rights Centre and is identified in the case materials as being associated with the Roma community. The case concerned the vulnerability of Roma individuals in the context of alleged failures by state authorities to effectively investigate a death, raising issues of potential exclusion from justice. The facts, as presented in the judgment, indicate that Ms. Djafer lodged an application under Article 2 of the European Convention on Human Rights, which protects the right to life, specifically complaining about the ineffective investigation into a death. The application was introduced on 15 January 2020, and the Government of North Macedonia subsequently offered a friendly settlement. Under the terms of this settlement, the Government agreed to pay Ms. Djafer 12,000 euros for non-pecuniary damage and costs, with the payment to be made within three months. The European Court of Human Rights, satisfied that the settlement respected human rights as defined by the Convention, struck the case out of its list in accordance with Article 39. The judgment does not contain any specific remarks or findings that distinguish this case beyond the friendly settlement procedure.
